Text: The standard Java console entry point is {{c1::public static void main(String[] args)}}.
Extra: The JVM looks for a compatible main method when launching the class.

Text: Most Java statements end with a {{c1::semicolon}}.
Extra: Missing semicolons are common beginner compile errors.

Text: Java blocks are enclosed in {{c1::curly braces}}: `{` and `}`.
Extra: Blocks define structure and often define scope.

Text: Java is {{c1::case-sensitive}}, so `Student` and `student` are different identifiers.
Extra: Capitalization matters in class, method, and variable names.

Text: Java class names usually use {{c1::PascalCase}}, while method and variable names usually use {{c2::camelCase}}.
Extra: Example: `StudentService` and `calculateTotal`.

Text: Java constants usually use {{c1::UPPER_SNAKE_CASE}}.
Extra: Example: `MAX_RETRY_COUNT`.

Text: A Java {{c1::package}} groups related classes and helps avoid name conflicts.
Extra: Package names are usually lowercase.

Text: An {{c1::import}} statement lets code use a class from another package by its simple name.
Extra: It does not copy code into the file.

Text: If a top-level class is `public`, the file name must match the {{c1::public class name}}.
Extra: Example: `public class HelloWorld` belongs in `HelloWorld.java`.

Text: A Java statement is usually ended with a {{c1::semicolon}}.
Extra: The semicolon marks the statement boundary.

Text: The JVM calls `main` without creating an object because `main` is {{c1::static}}.
Extra: Static methods belong to the class.

Text: The `String[] args` parameter receives {{c1::command-line arguments}}.
Extra: Arguments passed after the class name arrive as strings.

Text: Java single-line comments start with {{c1:://}}.
Extra: They continue until the end of the line.

Text: Java multi-line comments start with {{c1::/*}} and end with {{c2::*/}}.
Extra: Useful for longer comments, but avoid comment clutter.

Text: Java documentation comments start with {{c1::/**}} and can be used by `javadoc`.
Extra: They are common for public APIs.

Text: Package names are usually {{c1::lowercase}} and often use reversed domain style.
Extra: Example: `com.example.learning`.

Text: `import java.util.*` does {{c1::not}} import subpackages such as `java.util.concurrent`.
Extra: Wildcard imports only cover direct types in that package.

Text: Java class names usually use {{c1::PascalCase}}.
Extra: Example: `StudentService`.

Text: Java method and variable names usually use {{c1::camelCase}}.
Extra: Example: `calculateTotal`.

Text: Java keywords are {{c1::reserved words}} and cannot be used as identifiers.
Extra: Example keyword: `class`.

Text: A variable declared inside an `if` block is visible only inside that {{c1::block}}.
Extra: This is a scope rule.
